Whole Bay Area · times verified on each venue’s own page

This Week in the Bay

Tuesday–Sunday, September 22–27, 2026 · SF · East Bay · South Bay · North Bay

The week fall actually starts. The Symphony opens its season with Hilary Hahn, A.C.T. raises the curtain on Emma Rice’s North by Northwest, and the Australian Ballet brings the North American premiere of Oscar to Zellerbach with a live orchestra. Chuseok and the Mid-Autumn moon both land on Friday, so there is a Korean harvest festival on the Presidio lawn and a moon-festival night market on Irving Street. The San Francisco Electronic Music Festival turns 25, Maker Faire turns 20, SF Open Studios turns 52, and a brand-new film-restoration festival opens at the Roxie. Meanwhile Filoli lights a thousand jack-o’-lanterns, Lick Observatory closes its summer season on Mount Hamilton, and the Matisse that scandalized Paris leaves SFMOMA on Sunday. Filter by day and by region.

Big Museums

12 shows

Thursday is absurdly dense — After Dark, NightLife, mahjong at the Asian and a live podcast at SFMOMA all on the same night. Saturday is the cheap day: both FAMSF museums are free to Bay Area residents. Two closings to watch: the Matisse goes Sunday, and Cal Academy’s Tiny Chef ends Sept 30.

Ha Chong-Hyun: Retrospective

Asian Art Museum, 200 Larkin St, Civic Center

Sixty years of the Dansaekhwa pioneer who pushes oil through burlap from behind the canvas, so the paint arrives on the front as a kind of slow bruise. His first retrospective-scale showing in North America, opening the same weekend the museum celebrates Chuseok.

SF Open Studios begins its 52nd year, and the preview show that helps you plan it closes the same Sunday. Friday night YBCA opens two major shows on one ticket; Saturday afternoon the whole 25th Street corridor in Oakland is live; Sunday, Cushion Works runs two unrelated receptions at once.

Classical, Opera & Jazz

12 concerts

The season opens: the Symphony’s gala, two operas in repertory at the War Memorial, Opera San José’s first new Don Giovanni in twelve years, and a four-night Miles Davis centennial at SFJAZZ. Sunday afternoon is impossibly crowded — two operas, two orchestras and two recitals all start between 2 and 4pm.

🎭
TOP PICK★ SF CLASSICAL VOICE✦ Rarely staged
OperaThu & Sat 7:30pm

Mary, Queen of Scots (Thea Musgrave)

War Memorial Opera House, Civic Center
San Francisco
From $30 · sung in English, ~3 hrs

SF Opera gave this its American premiere in 1978 and has barely been staged in full in the States since. Now Musgrave is 98 and finally gets a mainstage revival, in a new co-production with English National Opera. SF Classical Voice calls it “hair-raising, dramatically harrowing — the tension never lets up.” Heidi Stober sings Mary; Clelia Cafiero conducts.

Repertory Cinema

13 screenings

An extraordinary week. The San Francisco Film Preserve launches Re:Vision, an entire festival of new restorations and rediscoveries — fourteen programs, eighteen countries, three of them on 35mm. Around it: Antonioni restored, Murnau with a live orchestra, and Bullitt screened from a boat on the bay it was filmed beside.

🎬
TOP PICK✦ 35mm + live quintet
Silent · 35mmSun 3:40pm

The Garden of Eden (Lewis Milestone, 1928)

Roxie Theater, Mission
San Francisco
$25 · $20 members

Re:Vision’s crown jewel: a silent proto-screwball newly restored by the SF Film Preserve with the Eastman Museum and the Library of Congress, shown on a film print with live accompaniment by the Club Foot Quintet. Montreal’s censors once ordered the last reel destroyed.

Notes & things to double-check

Times were read off each venue’s own event page on September 21, 2026. Confirm before you go: Chabot’s free telescope nights, Foothill Observatory and the stargazing half of Lick Observatory are clear-sky-only — Chabot closes its domes above ~90% humidity and posts live conditions at chabotspace.org/weather-station; Chabot itself is closed Wed 23 and Thu 24 for staff training, and Cal Academy’s Morrison Planetarium is closed through Wed 23; the Exploratorium’s Tactile Dome is shut Sept 8–28, so After Dark won’t include it; Boris Cherny at the Computer History Museum is full in person — waitlist and livestream only; R.F. Kuang, Jack White at City Lights and Clio’s Against Tech Oligarchy are all sold out or at capacity, and are listed only so you know they exist; Shotgun’s The Fall Show publishes no curtain time for its first two previews — call the box office (510.841.6500 x303); and City Lights’ Of Poetry & Protest 10th-anniversary reading on Sat 26 has been postponed. A few cards are imageless because the source ships no share image — chiefly the Bay Improviser listings, The Marsh, and several observatory and Hiller pages. Those show the clean category gradient.

Deliberately deprioritized / skipped

Per your anti-preferences: the Portola Festival (Pier 80, Sat–Sun) and Steve Aoki’s Dim Mak 30th at Bill Graham (EDM); Jack Harlow, T-Pain in Golden Gate Park, Eagles of Death Metal and Slayyyter (arena/club pop); DNA Lounge’s entire Fri–Sun slate (DJ nights); the Oddities & Curiosities Expo and the ADU & Tiny Home Expo (expos); assorted trivia nights, bar crawls and networking mixers. Folsom Street Fair (Sun 27) and the Bay Area Queer Zine Fest are skipped as Pride/identity-framed, per the same list. Also left out: routine first-run multiplex showtimes, and ODC’s Fall for Art at di Rosa in Napa — a lovely site-specific performance, but it is a $750-a-head fundraising gala rather than a ticket.

Coverage

Every source row in sources.md was scanned — fifteen categories, read with each row’s own reader. Legitimately empty this week: CounterPulse (dark all September), Root Division and Southern Exposure (between shows), Moe’s, Marcus and Walden Pond Books, The Tech Interactive, Long Now, JCCSF, Central Works and PlayGround SF. Alameda Point Antiques Faire (1st Sun) and Oakland Vintage Market (1st Sat) do not fall in this window; the next ones are Oct 4 and Oct 3.

Built for andrew@antimatter.io · the whole Bay Area · Tuesday–Sunday, September 22–27, 2026
